John Wayne cut or John F. Kennedy is intriguing.

lamNotARobot 2 January, 2017 at 09:02
It seems like Panini is inundating the market with repetitive products that lack originality or
style.

2.
Barts March, 2017 at 15:08
Welcome to the world of “exclusive license” agreements
3.
Mike C11 March, 2017 at 13:09
Remember when trading cards were... ehh, what’s the word.. FUN to collect??? When there
was maybe 3 or 4 sets, one always better than the rest, only 3-4 versions ALL TOGETHER
of pulling that rookie everyone wanted, skyrotting excitement and anticipation??? Now it’s
just stressful, confusing, redundant, you're all but guaranteed to pull at least one VERSION
of said hot card.. problem is.. there ends up being 60 versions... problem is, everyone gets A
VERSION, problem is, IT SUCKS.. good job, way to inherit awesomeness and kill everything
awesome about it..
fe}
Ryan Cracknellii March, 2017 at 13:43
If you’re collecting for fun, I’m guessing you’re approaching it as a hobby. Hobby’s
shouldn't be stressful. They should be the opposite. While there are lots of products
out there, stick to the ones that interest you and don’t worry about the rest. All of a
sudden that big list is smaller, more manageable and probably more fun again. The
days of being able to get EVERYTHING disappeared about 25 years ago.

4.
John Bateman March, 2017 at 22:36
Yes 1992 — that was about it. This is an amazing amount of rookie cards — some only
autographed only — no one could put one set together but maybe the next Tom Brady is
hidden in there.

Oh great, another over priced, minimum card, one pack, over high end product. Like we dont
already have enough of them. Just kill the hobby then

Goodballcards14 May, 2017 at 21:23
Doesn't look like any on-card autographs. Am | seeing that right? If so a lot of folks might
pass. No Gold Strike. No Gold AU. A lot of sideways stuff as well. Hope there is more too it
than what's showing here...

3.
IAMNotARoboto May, 2017 at 08:36
In the late 80’s and early 90’s, overproduction killed some companies. Can alleged ‘high-
end’, expensive products have a similar effect on the hobby in the long run? Panini is getting
so gimmicky — copying (almost exactly) Topps products, adding gems (why???) and
extremely limited products (Gala, with a print run of only 8 rookie cards — c’mon man!!) The
lack of competition may just be this hobby’s undoing.

4.
Kerry 11 July, 2017 at 17:26
If high-end products are offered like this, then why not just issue 100 or so cards of the
greatest players and let everyone with big bucks enjoy ripping open the big players? | have
seen too many high-end box breaks with sub-par player autos or parallels that nobody
(except relatives) want.

Kerry! July, 2017 at 17:28

3.
IAMNotARoboto May, 2017 at 08:36
In the late 80’s and early 90’s, overproduction killed some companies. Can alleged ‘high-
end’, expensive products have a similar effect on the hobby in the long run? Panini is getting
so gimmicky — copying (almost exactly) Topps products, adding gems (why???) and
extremely limited products (Gala, with a print run of only 8 rookie cards — c’mon man!!) The
lack of competition may just be this hobby’s undoing.

(except relatives) want.

Dylan Horn)? May, 2017 at 21:02
Oh great, another over priced, minimum card, one pack, over high end product. Like we dont
already have enough of them. Just kill the hobby then

2.
Goodballcards14 May, 2017 at 21:23
Doesn't look like any on-card autographs. Am | seeing that right? If so a lot of folks might
pass. No Gold Strike. No Gold AU. A lot of sideways stuff as well. Hope there is more too it
than what's showing here...

3.
IAMNotARoboto May, 2017 at 08:36
In the late 80’s and early 90’s, overproduction killed some companies. Can alleged ‘high-
end’, expensive products have a similar effect on the hobby in the long run? Panini is getting
so gimmicky — copying (almost exactly) Topps products, adding gems (why???) and
extremely limited products (Gala, with a print run of only 8 rookie cards — c’mon man!!) The
lack of competition may just be this hobby’s undoing.

4.
Kerry 11 July, 2017 at 17:26
If high-end products are offered like this, then why not just issue 100 or so cards of the
greatest players and let everyone with big bucks enjoy ripping open the big players? | have
seen too many high-end box breaks with sub-par player autos or parallels that nobody
(except relatives) want.

5.
Kerry! July, 2017 at 17:28
| mean, enough already with autos of Paul Perkins and Leonte Carroo!

end retail product.

5.
Marks December, 2024 at 20:24
Would the players collection (3 patches) worth more than most rookie premium patches
since they are so scarce for a lot players? Since Mahomes is the famous player of this year,
we will use him as an example. The players collection autographed Mahomes (25 ) standard,
(2) gold and (1) 1/1 platinum = 28 total copies of 2017 Immaculate Copies.
While all the copies of all other Panini products typically have more copies in any set.
Example, the most popular 2017 National Treasure auto # 161 has 99 standard, 25 silver, 13
stars and stripe, 10 gold, 5 black, 2 Red, and 1 platinum for a total 155 copies. Not as scarce
even though it is considered as premium tier brand compared to immaculate. Why is the 28
scarce copies not as valuable as flawless and national treasure when their hobby box is
close in cost?

5.
Marks December, 2024 at 20:24
Would the players collection (3 patches) worth more than most rookie premium patches
since they are so scarce for a lot players? Since Mahomes is the famous player of this year,
we will use him as an example. The players collection autographed Mahomes (25 ) standard,
(2) gold and (1) 1/1 platinum = 28 total copies of 2017 Immaculate Copies.
While all the copies of all other Panini products typically have more copies in any set.
Example, the most popular 2017 National Treasure auto # 161 has 99 standard, 25 silver, 13
stars and stripe, 10 gold, 5 black, 2 Red, and 1 platinum for a total 155 copies. Not as scarce
even though it is considered as premium tier brand compared to immaculate. Why is the 28
scarce copies not as valuable as flawless and national treasure when their hobby box is
close in cost?

5.

Marks December, 2024 at 20:24
Would the players collection (3 patches) worth more than most rookie premium patches
since they are so scarce for a lot players? Since Mahomes is the famous player of this year,
we will use him as an example. The players collection autographed Mahomes (25 ) standard,
(2) gold and (1) 1/1 platinum = 28 total copies of 2017 Immaculate Copies.
While all the copies of all other Panini products typically have more copies in any set.
Example, the most popular 2017 National Treasure auto # 161 has 99 standard, 25 silver, 13
stars and stripe, 10 gold, 5 black, 2 Red, and 1 platinum for a total 155 copies. Not as scarce
even though it is considered as premium tier brand compared to immaculate. Why is the 28
scarce copies not as valuable as flawless and national treasure when their hobby box is
close in cost?
